task.title: Weighted cyclic dispatch
task.specification: Config weights maps tenant IDs to positive integers. Build a fixed slot cycle by sorted tenant ID, repeating each tenant weight times. Start cursor=0 and empty per-tenant FIFO queues. Events add{tenant,id}, dispatch. Add rejects an id already pending in any tenant (status=duplicate); otherwise queues it (status=queued). Dispatch scans at most one cycle starting at cursor, takes the first nonempty tenant FIFO item, then sets cursor to the slot after that chosen slot modulo cycle length (status=sent). If all queues empty status=empty and cursor stays unchanged. Output {status,sent:id_or_null,queues:{every tenant:[pending IDs]},cursor}. Tenants always exist in config. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}; initial state is null. Only the current event is available; each named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"run"}. Inputs have at most eight single lowercase ASCII-letter identifiers, safe integer quantities and at most 48 events. Return exactly the documented output fields after every event; state representation is unrestricted JSON. All identifiers and numeric fields shown in event forms are present; quantities and all intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. Regimes vary event order and timing: ordinary uses moderate capacity, boundary tests equality/empty cases, adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events, and shift uses smaller capacities or larger costs/delays within the same semantics. Generator regimes: Boundary weights are a:1,b:3,c:1; shift weights a:2,b:1,c:3 replace ordinary a:1,b:2,c:1, with eight job IDs and 70% add events instead of four IDs and 50%. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Dendrochronology
matchedCard.relation: Overlapping sequences can be aligned by distinctive patterns spanning several observations. Cross-comparison can reveal missing or extra local observations that a simple position count would treat as elapsed intervals.
assumptions: The sequences share a comparable underlying history.
The overlap contains enough distinguishing structure to support alignment.
matchedCard.boundary: Repeated patterns or insufficient overlap can support several alignments. A single coincident observation does not establish a unique chronological match.
matchedCard.source_fact: NOAA describes crossdating tree-ring patterns from several trees to account for missing or extra rings and align samples from different periods.

shuffledCard.label: Comparator hysteresis
shuffledCard.relation: A state-dependent comparator uses distinct upper and lower transition thresholds. Between them, the existing state is retained. Fluctuations that remain within this interval need not cause repeated switching.
assumptions: The output has a preceding state.
Distinct thresholds are appropriate to the signal range and acceptable response delay.
shuffledCard.boundary: A wider separation can postpone response to a real change. Behavior with two state-dependent thresholds differs from reacting to every crossing of one fixed threshold.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Texas Instruments describes an inverting comparator with upper and lower hysteresis thresholds to reduce unwanted transitions caused by noise or slow-moving signals.

initial.explanation: Use the target's weighted cyclic scheduler directly. Cursor is a slot index; each dispatch scans one complete cycle and advances only after sending. Duplicate detection scans all pending queues, while sent IDs cease being pending.
initial.mapping: config.weights determines sorted tenant order and repeated slot array; state stores that array, cursor, and tenant FIFO queues. Each output mirrors queues and cursor after the event.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated validity constraints. The conditional rule applies to every legal public trace and checks the documented transition semantics.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var w=input.config.weights,ts=Object.keys(w).sort(),s=[],q={};for(var i=0;i<ts.length;i++){q[ts[i]]=[];for(var j=0;j<w[ts[i]];j++)s.push(ts[i]);}var c=0;for(var k=0;k<input.events.length;k++){var e=input.events[k],o=output[k],sent=null,st;if(e.type==='add'){var d=false;for(var t of ts)if(q[t].indexOf(e.id)>=0)d=true;if(d)st='duplicate';else{q[e.tenant].push(e.id);st='queued';}}else{st='empty';if(s.length)for(var z=0;z<s.length;z++){var x=(c+z)%s.length;if(q[s[x]].length){sent=q[s[x]].shift();c=(x+1)%s.length;st='sent';break;}}}var qq={};for(var t of ts)qq[t]=q[t].slice();if(!o||o.status!==st||o.sent!==sent||o.cursor!==c||JSON.stringify(o.queues)!==JSON.stringify(qq))return false;}return true;}
initial.program: function solve(x){var cfg=x.config,e=x.event,st=x.state,ts=Object.keys(cfg.weights).sort(),s,q,c;if(st===null){s=[];q={};for(var i=0;i<ts.length;i++){q[ts[i]]=[];for(var j=0;j<cfg.weights[ts[i]];j++)s.push(ts[i]);}c=0;}else{s=st.s;q=st.q;c=st.c;}var status,sent=null;if(e.type==='add'){var dup=false;for(var i=0;i<ts.length;i++)if(q[ts[i]].indexOf(e.id)!==-1){dup=true;break;}if(dup)status='duplicate';else{q[e.tenant].push(e.id);status='queued';}}else{status='empty';if(s.length)for(var z=0;z<s.length;z++){var p=(c+z)%s.length,t=s[p];if(q[t].length){sent=q[t].shift();c=(p+1)%s.length;status='sent';break;}}}var queues={};for(var i=0;i<ts.length;i++)queues[ts[i]]=q[ts[i]].slice();return {state:{s:s,q:q,c:c},output:{status:status,sent:sent,queues:queues,cursor:c}}}

final.explanation: Maintains a repeated-slot cycle, per-tenant FIFO queues, and the current cursor in opaque state. Add events reject IDs found in any pending queue. Dispatch examines at most one complete cycle from the cursor, removes the first available FIFO item, and advances to the following slot; empty dispatches leave the cursor unchanged.

initial.explanation: Use weighted cyclic scheduling: sorted tenant IDs expand into slots, and the cursor marks the next slot to inspect. Add preserves FIFO order and rejects any pending ID globally. Dispatch scans at most one cycle, removes the first available item, and advances immediately after its selected slot.
initial.mapping: Tenants map to queues; weights map to repeated cycle slots; cursor maps to the next scan position; pending maps IDs to their owning tenant for global duplicate detection.
initial.assumptions: Tenant IDs and job IDs are lowercase ASCII strings, weights are positive safe integers, and events conform to the documented add/dispatch forms.

final.explanation: Build the sorted weighted slot cycle on each step. State stores tenant FIFO queues, a global pending-ID map, and the next cursor. Adds reject any own pending-ID entry; dispatch scans at most one cycle, removes the first available FIFO item, and advances to the slot after the chosen slot. Output queues are copied so the returned output is a snapshot.
